column1: # Phi-Pill Line and Phi-Pill Link: watch-face numerals and the letters a
# dial needs, after the outline numerals of the Hermès Apple Watch face
# (the user, 27 November 2026) but drawn on the house's construction,
# never traced. `line.py` builds both families from these rows alone.
# One construction, the one Phi-Pill is made on: a closed outline led
# from corner to corner, each corner as round as its radius says (as
# appkit's `script/icon.py` reads a `fill`), every round a true circle,
# each circle joined to the next by the line that touches both (as
# Phiogy's `script/chain.py` draws). Two corners of the same circle (a
# bar's end, a link's end) become that one circle: a pill.
# Phi-Pill Link fills the outline. Phi-Pill Line draws the outline only,
# as one thin line with every turn round: the outline taken out by half
# the line and in by half the line, the same circles with their radii
# grown and shrunk, so every curve of the line is still a true arc.
#   take  read from a Phi-Pill file: `FILE GLYPH what`, what being
#         cap (the file's cap height), top (the glyph's highest ink),
#         wide (its ink's width), or `y|x AT ink|gap K`: a straight cut
#         across the glyph at AT, and the K-th run of ink (or of space
#         between inks) it meets, counted from 0
#   let   a measure made of others: + - * / and brackets, no spaces
#   face  `line|solid STYLE WEIGHT`: the family in the name column
# The glyphs (the outline's corners `x y r`, apart by commas, taken with
# the clock, y up from the baseline, x from the glyph's first ink):
#   wide    the ink's width; the side bearing is Phi-Pill's either side
#   cut     the outline of a space inside it, also taken with the clock
#   turn    another glyph's outlines turned half round (9 is 6 turned)
#   mirror  another glyph's outlines mirrored left to right (5 is 2)
# --- measures, from Phi-Pill Regular (Light for the line) ---
# where the middle bars sit: Phi-Pill's 8 and hyphen hang theirs at mid
# a link's end, half the bowl's height (6, 9); a's bowl holds one round
# space, so its link is two bars and a counter high (a, and e its turn)
# s: two bowls, each turn half a bowl round
# the narrower letters (j l r t) leave out a bar's width
# m and w: Phi-Pill's own narrower stems and counters
# v: where the stems bend so the foot is one round of half a stem
# --- numerals: every one as wide as 0, so a dial's figures line up ---
